rule_friction.idea: Fold the objective's products into the step pass, or skip recomputing products the step pass already computed, saving most of the roughly 42 us per iteration the objective costs
rule_friction.rule: `fom_objective.c` is fixed and must be called as is

rule_friction.idea: Store the factor panel in float32 to halve its 2.5 MB of traffic
rule_friction.rule: `make verify` requires solving the same system with the given factorization, and it would lose accuracy

rule_friction.idea: Specialize `step_su__rest` / `t0_state` to their fixed small-row patterns, such as 1–2 entries per row with constant ±1/scaled structure (the matrices are scaled identity/difference blocks per spec.json)
rule_friction.rule: `fom_ops.c` may not hardcode coefficients, so this needs runtime-derived structure tables that `fom_setup` cannot build through the ops entry points

rule_friction.idea: Gather the panel's group sums directly while doing the forward head pass, using a single combined buffer between the solve and the rhs
rule_friction.rule: only the `fom_lin_solve_t0(b, x)` signature is exposed; no cross-call workspace in `include/`

rule_friction.idea: Inline or cheapen the per-check verification objective (13.4%)
rule_friction.rule: `src/fom_objective.c` is fixed and must not be reimplemented

rule_friction.idea: Store the dense LDLT panel (P_DAT) in float32 or compressed form to halve the bandwidth-bound panel traffic (about 21%)
rule_friction.rule: must apply the same factorization exactly (and accuracy)

rule_friction.idea: Build the ELL copies in `fom_setup` instead of lazily on first call
rule_friction.rule: `fom_ops.c` has no setup hook, and the header and signature files are fixed

rule_friction.idea: Store the dense 3000x101 panel of the t0 factor in float32 (or use mixed precision) to halve the bandwidth of the two hottest regions
rule_friction.rule: target constraints / "apply that factorization" (changes the factor's values, so accuracy is no longer guaranteed)

rule_friction.idea: Speed up or cut the cost of `fom_objective` (fuse its products with `step_su`/`step_t1`, which read the same state and t0 data)
rule_friction.rule: fom_objective.c is fixed and must not be reimplemented or inlined

rule_friction.idea: Fold the input/output permutation of the t0 solve into the `rhs_t0` and `step_*` kernels (write the rhs already permuted)
rule_friction.rule: fom_lin_solve_t0 signature fixed and checked directly against the reference solve; solver may not read matrix data to build a permuted operator

rule_friction.idea: Store the 2.4 MB dense panel in float32 (or float32 plus a correction) to halve L2 traffic in ls_fpanel and ls_bpanel
rule_friction.rule: must solve the same system with the given factorization in fom_float (target precision / correctness)

rule_friction.idea: Split the panel passes across 2 cores (each pass is L2-bandwidth-bound on one core)
rule_friction.rule: fixed Makefile/build flags (no threads) and embedded target constraints

rule_friction.idea: Make the objective's sparse loops faster (19.5% of runtime: about 1.1 ms per call, every 25 iterations)
rule_friction.rule: `src/fom_objective.c` is fixed and the metric may not be reimplemented
